704476.t: Traditionally taken as a nominal formation from εἰλέω (eiléō, “to turn, wind”) (< *ϝελ-νέ-ω (*wel-né-ō)) with a suffix -ιξ (-ix), as seen also in ἧλιξ (hêlix, “of the same age”), χόλιξ (khólix, “guts”), δέλφιξ (délphix, “tripod”), further from…

704438.t: Earlier form: Mycenaean Greek 𐀁𐀩𐀞 (e-re-pa /⁠elephās⁠/). Probably borrowed from Egyptian ꜣbw Ab-b-w-E26 (reconstructed as earlier /ˈʀuːbaw/, later /ˈjuːbə/)..

704428.t: From Proto-Hellenic *eléutʰeros, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁léwdʰeros, from *h₁lewdʰ- (“to grow up; people, tribe”); the original meaning of the word was "belonging to the tribe".

704426.t: Unclear. Could be related to ἐλελεῦ (eleleû, “woe, alas”), which is likely expressive or onomatopoeic.

704436.t: From ἐλέφας (eléphas, “elephant”) + -ινος (-inos, “-ine”). Compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀁𐀩𐀞𐀳𐀃 (e-re-pa-te-o), 𐀁𐀩𐀞𐀳𐀍 (e-re-pa-te-jo, “made of ivory”) formed with -εῖος (-eîos).
